thesis: ExxonMobil has told the market it will hit $20B of structural savings by 2030 and run a single SAP S/4HANA instance by 2028, while cutting about 2,000 roles and centralizing IT. The ~65M lines of ECC6 custom code are on the critical path to both commitments. Devin is the extra engineering capacity that turns the custom-code triage, remediation and testing from SI hours into a measured, parallel workload, and the savings show up on the ledger the CFO already reports.

why_now.t: The 2028 S/4HANA target means custom-code decisions get made in the next 12-18 months, whether or not Devin is involved.
The new CFO, Neil Hansen, ran Global Business Solutions (GBS), the group that owns the ERP and process program. The economic sponsor already knows the pain first-hand.
$16.3B of the $20B savings is banked. The last $3.7B is the hardest, and workforce cuts are a named lever, so capacity without headcount fits the plan.
Centralization into Global Operations plus the Budapest, Bengaluru and Buenos Aires centers concentrates engineering decisions in fewer hands, so fewer people need to say yes.
Four IT leaders are new in role (Brad Harris, Ryan Seager, James Lynch and others), and new leaders set new agendas.

challenges.stated: Consolidate 12 ERP systems into one SAP S/4HANA instance by 2028. The CEO says it is 'already delivering results'.
challenges.devin: Devin and Code Scans inventory and classify custom objects and interfaces as retire, rewrite or keep, then parallel Devins remediate and test them.

challenges.stated: About 65M lines of custom ECC6 code, which the CFO called a record among SAP customers, plus a decades-old consolidation mainframe to retire.
challenges.devin: Legacy analysis and documentation at codebase scale, plus mainframe and interface rewrites with tests and recordings as proof of work.

challenges.stated: $20B structural cost savings vs 2019 by 2030, with operational efficiencies and workforce reductions named as drivers.
challenges.devin: Count Devin output in SI and contractor hours avoided, so it maps straight onto the savings ledger.

challenges.stated: Cut ~2,000 jobs by end-2027 and centralize ops, projects, technology and supply chain.
challenges.devin: Keeps the backlog from growing as headcount falls, and captures legacy-system knowledge in DeepWiki and Knowledge before people leave.

challenges.stated: The board treats cyber as a priority: the VP of IT runs the cybersecurity program, and the Audit Committee reviews it every year.
challenges.devin: Each Devin runs in its own isolated machine, and every change comes with recorded proof of work. That gives the cyber review an audit trail instead of a black box.

challenges.stated: 'Technology-led business with structurally stronger earnings power.'
challenges.devin: This is the CEO's own phrase. Use it to frame Devin as a technology lever on earnings, not an IT tool.

pain_chain.pain: $20B savings and the 2030 plan depend on finishing the ERP consolidation on time.
The S/4HANA date is at risk from custom-code volume and SI capacity, and IT headcount is falling.
pain_chain.measure: Program milestones; SI run-rate; cyber findings open

pain_chain.level: L3 IT Global Projects / Business Transformation directors
pain_chain.pain: Custom-code triage and interface rewrites are slower than planned, and testing is the bottleneck.
pain_chain.measure: Objects triaged per week; defects found in test; cutover readiness

pain_chain.level: L4 SAP technical leads, GBC engineering managers
pain_chain.pain: Undocumented ABAP, a shrinking pool of people who know it, and manual regression testing.
pain_chain.measure: Hours per object; review backlog; on-call pages

com.elevator: You've committed $20B of structural savings and a single S/4HANA instance by 2028, with fewer people. Devin is an autonomous AI software engineer that works through the custom-code and interface backlog in parallel, in isolated machines, with proof of work on every change. That moves the date in and the SI spend down.
before: 65M lines of custom code triaged mostly by people, with SI teams billing by the hour
Interface and mainframe rewrites queued behind a shrinking IT bench
Coding assistants in the IDE, if any, that don't move whole migration tasks
Cyber and OT security reviews slow down anything 'AI' that touches code
negative: S/4HANA dates slip, legacy ECC6 and the mainframe run in parallel for longer, and dual-running costs eat into savings
SI change orders grow the run-and-maintain line
Knowledge of legacy systems leaves with the people being cut
Regulatory and cyber exposure from rushed, under-tested cutover code
after: Every custom object classified and documented, with a remediation plan per object
Rewrite and test work running in parallel across Devins, with recordings for reviewers
SI hours and dual-running months come off the savings ledger
A governed, auditable AI engineering pattern IT can reuse across Upstream IT and the GBCs
required: Runs in isolated, customer-governed machines with no code leaving approved boundaries
Works at codebase scale: thousands of objects in parallel, deterministic and resumable
Proof of work: tests and recordings on every change, reviewed against their own standards
Fits the identity, repo and ticketing stack (SailPoint, ServiceNow, Kubernetes; confirm the SAP transport and CI path)
Spend tied to measured output, not seats
metrics: Custom objects triaged per week (baseline from the program office)
Hours per object remediated and tested vs SI baseline
Months of ECC6 and mainframe dual-running avoided
Mean time to close critical vulnerabilities in scoped repos
how: Code Scans to inventory and classify the estate
Dynamic Workflows to run parallel Devins over the object list
DeepWiki and Knowledge to capture legacy logic
Devin Review and recordings for proof of work
Isolated VMs on Windows and Linux for the security review
proof: Use the customer stories from the playbook: swarms (parallel migration), harness, security
Confirm ABAP and SAP-side support with the solutions engineer before you scope it

meddpicc.name: Decision process
meddpicc.known: AI governance and cyber review are almost certainly required, and OT has its own review.
meddpicc.next: Map the steps: tech eval, then cyber/AI governance, then architecture, then EB, then procurement.

meddpicc.known: Large-enterprise supplier onboarding; SAP and SI contracts in place.
meddpicc.gap: Paper process, vendor-onboarding lead time, MSA path (direct or via AWS Marketplace).

meddpicc.gap: Nobody has named a slipping milestone yet, or said who it hurts.

meddpicc.name: Champion
meddpicc.known: Shortlist from Sales Navigator: Aaron Surber (R2R IT, ERP consolidation), Neil Higgins (SAP Group Reporting), Ryan Seager (Global Ops IT projects). Paolo Biagi is a portfolio coach.

meddpicc.known: SAP tooling and SIs; a copilot and LLM foundation and a Gen AI org exist (Sales Nav). AWS confirmed; no Azure or GCP seen at leadership level.
meddpicc.gap: Whether coding is in scope for the existing AI program, and who the S/4 SI is.
meddpicc.next: Ask Mathews or Biagi whether coding agents are in scope. Lead with AWS, not a multi-cloud message.
